newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Rundle twins raise A$26 million.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Rundle twins raise A$26 million.

text.p: Shale oil hopefuls Central Pacific Petroleum NL and Southern Pacific Petroleum NL, the so-called Rundle twins, said on Tuesday they raised about A$26 million through the placement of shares and convertible notes to clients of stockbroker Wilson HTM.
Southern Pacific placed 3.25 million convertible unsecured notes at A$2.00 each to raise about A$6.5 million.
Central Pacific placed 2.9 million ordinary shares at A$4.50 per share and 1.3 million convertible unsecured notes at A$5.00 per note to raise a total of A$19.55 million.
Both issues are to augment working capital and are not related to securities to be issued to Canada's Suncor Inc, a spokesman for Southern Pacific Petroleum said.
On Monday, Suncor won Australian foreign investment approval to join the joint venture, formed to develop the Stuart oil shale deposit in central Queensland
Suncor will hold a 50 percent interest with Southern Pacific Petroleum and Central Pacific Minerals each holding 25 percent.
Suncor also won approval to acquire share interests in Southern Pacific and Central Pacific under terms approved by shareholders of the two companies last month, they said.
The terms will give Suncor about 22 percent interests in both companies excluding their cross shareholdings through the issue of Restricted Class Shares to Suncor.
The issue of the restricted class shares and Suncor's participation in the project will be subject to the financial close of the first of three stages of the project, they said.
Southern Pacific shares closed three cents lower at A$1.90 on turnover of 97,500 shares while Central Pacific shares were 10 cents lower at A$4.40 on turnover of 1,780 shares.
